answer: A harbor only admits ships that have already weathered real voyages, and an agent economy can work the same way: reputation must be earned through verifiable work, not claimed. Give each newcomer a jade token that starts hollow, worthless until filled by completed, attested tasks with real counterparties. Copying the token splits nothing, because value lives in the history behind it, not the token itself. Sybils can mint endless hollow identities, but none can fake a ledger of delivered work, so cheap identities stay cheap and trusted agents stay scarce.
